I honestly can't believe I haven't left a review for this game yet. My one issue with Terraria is it can be rather grindy at times, especially if you want a specific item or weapon and sometimes the bosses can feel a little unfair when playing by yourself. Other than that, there is a reason it's been around for over 15 years and remains peak. The Villager Npc's feel a lot more than just shopkeepers having histories, lore, and even relationships with the other villagers. (which I love despite making it sometimes hard to plan houses for them all). This is definitely a game to play WITH friends, but can be just as fun with yourself. The vast amount of bosses, and weapons you can use to disperse them are definitely a huge plus, allowing for creative and often absurd solutions that fit for your playing style. 

I won't deny that you likely do need a wiki for progression or crafting while planning as while as cool as this game is, I won't deny that it isn't the most beginner friendly. (Personally I like that though). I feel it has a lot to offer, whether its building beautiful castles and creations, or battling against cosmic entities, or a fishing sim, there is something for everyone!

Simply put, Terraria is one of if not the most enjoyable action sandbox game money can buy.
To explain the rough idea of Terraria it runs off of player curiosity and the natural urge to explore new things, you'll find yourself asking "What's this? or "Who's that?" or "Does this hurt me?" every moment you play. I'm aware of the turn offs such as "It's too grindy" or "There's no guide to progression" but thats the entire intent of Terraria, it's built for you to learn on your own through exploration, stay in certain areas to kill certain enemies for specific drops needed to progress. In nature this is a grindy and long-winded game but for all the right reasons. I'll keep it concise in a bullet point list as to what Terrarias progression looks like to the average player (my own time played totals to around 1.1k hours on Steam but 2k more on other devices).

Early Game (Pre-Boss):
- Make housing using the beginner tools provided
- Delve into the naturally spawning caves in search of loot
- Further explore each side of your world to find the two important early parts of Terraria (the jungle and the dungeon - they spawn on opposite sides of the world to each other - the jungle side towards the end near the ocean has an important but not necessary biome deep underground known as the shimmer, search it up if you want a deeper look)
- Prepare arenas for upcoming bosses and events

Mid Pre-Hardmode (Post Eye/Evil Boss/Queen Bee):
- Talk to that guy you may have met at the dungeon and summon his curse with your well-earned gear
- Explore the dungeons depths once you have beaten Skeletron
- Search the gold chests with the gold key drops (can drop from dungeon pots, dungeon enemies, dungeon slimes most commonly or rarely wood chests in the dungeon)
- Grab your dungeon loot alongside the possibility of an obsidian key to unlock those locked chests in hell if you've stumbled into there yet
- Grab your hell loot from the chests and build a long platform in hell, you're gonna need it

End Pre-Hardmode:
- Find a guide voodoo doll dropped from voodoo demons in hell into a pocket of lava, if you can't get this to drop make a house for the guide to move in just above hell and cause him to fall into lava in hell
- Kill the Wall of Flesh and you're officially halfway through the game (at least in my eyes)

I'll leave it at this as to not ruin the exciting changes hardmode brings, bare in mind hardmode is not a difficulty changer but does bring stronger enemies while keeping the previous ones you've fought. Message me if you'd like someone to help bring you into this game (I love teaching others to play this game thats given me endless wonder for many years and many more to come).

If you end up beating Terraria and doing everything you want to, Great! Theres a wonderful modding community over at tModLoader that has endless content for you to enjoy (I'm making my own mod but my personal favourite choice is the Calamity Mod that practically doubles Terrarias content).

I hope I was convincing enough, please do buy this game we need to crack top ten games of all time. <3
